c.tagline: The Silk Road's blue-domed jewel, capital of Timur's empire.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmarked private cars with no meter; agree the fare before getting in, or use the Yandex Go app for a fixed, fair price. Rides across the city are very cheap.

emergency.note: Dial 101 for fire, 102 for police and 103 for ambulance; 112 also works as a unified emergency number.

avoid.reason: Expect taxi overcharging and souvenir hard-selling around the Registan and Siyob Bazaar; agree prices before rides or purchases.

hood_desc: The monumental heart of Samarkand around Registan Square's three tiled madrasas, with Gur-e-Amir (Timur's tomb) a short walk away; the classic first-timer base, ringed by boutique hotels and B&Bs within walking distance of the icons.

The leafy pedestrian avenue (Universitet Xiyoboni) lined with cafes, fountains, hotels and restaurants connecting the old city to the modern town; a convenient, lively, walkable base with the widest choice of dining.

The atmospheric old-town quarter around the colossal Bibi-Khanym Mosque and the bustling Siyob Bazaar, with the tiled Shah-i-Zinda necropolis nearby; best for market life, street food and being steps from the sights.

A large modern tourism resort and eco-park north of the center built around an artificial lake, with international five-star hotels, the Eternal City heritage park, a spa and conference venues; suits travelers wanting polished resort comfort over old-town character.
A quieter modern residential district with everyday shops, local restaurants and mid-range hotels away from the tourist core; suits longer stays and budget travelers wanting a calmer, local base.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.hours: Buses and marshrutka minibuses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; Yandex Go taxis fill the late-night gaps.
transit.note: Samarkand has no metro or tram; travel is by city buses, shared marshrutka minibuses and cheap taxis (book via Yandex Go for a fixed fare). The major monuments cluster within a walkable historic core.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash or by Uzcard/Humo card to the driver (about 1,700 so'm). Taxis are cheap; agree the fare in advance or use the app.

bus: Intercity buses & shared taxis to Bukhara, Tashkent and Shakhrisabz
train: Afrosiyob & Sharq trains (Samarkand station) to Tashkent, Bukhara and Khiva

transit.m: City bus / marshrutka minibus to the center (~30 min)
Taxi or Yandex Go to the center (15-20 min)

tip.r: Not expected; upscale restaurants may add a 10-15% service charge, otherwise rounding up the bill is enough.
